Updated: 10:31 PM CDT Apr 20, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ For hours Monday, Milwaukee police detectives and crews used a bobcat and other specialized equipment to search in, under and around a garage behind a home on the city's far north side.News Chopper 12 captured investigators cutting the concrete floor behind the home near 15th and Congress streets, and removed it in chunks. Later, those crews could be seen hauling out large quantities of soil.A department spokesperson would only say the activity was part of an ongoing investigation as detectives executed a search warrant. The official did not reveal the subject of the investigation and what police were searching for.Late Monday, the spokesperson said police had not found any remains, but said the investigation is ongoing. The home was connected to a car theft and arson investigation, according to a search warrant filed in January 2026. In the document, a detective said investigators were searching for cellphones, tablets a computer and gun ammunition at the time the warrant was filed.In 2007, the home was the listed address of Michael Lock, when prosecutors charged the notorious drug dealer with two murders. The charges followed the 2005 discovery of the body of Felipe Armondo Melendez-Rivas, one of Lock's rival drug dealers, under a concrete slab at a home on Fiebrantz Avenue.The same 2007 criminal complaint said investigators also discovered the buried remains of Eugene Chaney, another drug rival to Lock. A jury convicted Lock of the two murders. He is serving life sentences.Still, police have not confirmed whether Monday's search is connected to Lock and his criminal cases, the January search warrant or another case.Searching at the property is expected to resume Tuesday.This is a developing story.Top HeadlinesDog rescued from Milwaukee apartment fire near Holy Cross CemeteryFather, son rescued after kayak overturns on Milwaukee RiverAnimal activists attempt to break into Ridglan Farms a second timeWATCH Horse rescued after flooding in Milwaukee MILWAUKEE —For hours Monday, Milwaukee police detectives and crews used a bobcat and other specialized equipment to search in, under and around a garage behind a home on the city's far north side.News Chopper 12 captured investigators cutting the concrete floor behind the home near 15th and Congress streets, and removed it in chunks. It happened Monday morning in the San Fernando Valley community of Pacoima, California. Video shows a low-flying plane strike a power line, triggering a small explosion, before plummeting about 30 feet to a parking lot below. According to officials with the Los Angeles Fire Department, a 70-year-old man was flying the Cessna 172.After striking the power line, the plane nosedived into an O'Reilly’s auto shop parking lot below.Local news outlets report that the plane was returning to the nearby Whiteman Airport at the time of the crash. The pilot, who was the only person in the plane, was taken to a nearby hospital for treatment. His condition is unknown.No additional injuries were reported.Officials with the Federal Aviation Administration say the crash is under investigation. Piscatella has spent more than 90 years serving the Catholic Church, joining the Dominican order when she was 17. Above video: Study confirms being grateful may help you live longerThe Long Island native has been a member of the Sisters of St. Dominic of Amityville since 1931. Through her decades of service, Piscatella served as a teacher, taking on various subjects in Catholic schools across the area until she retired at 84. In fact, teaching is the secret to longevity, according to Piscatella."Teach until you die," she told the New York Post in 2025, when asked about her secret to a long and healthy life.“You have to be a saint before you get to heaven,” she said.Piscatella has seen 10 different popes in her lifetime. And in celebration of her 113th birthday, Pope Leo XIV issued a proclamation celebrating her milestone birthday, according to WABC-TV in New York.Piscatella has held the title of the world's oldest living nun for a little over a year now, according to Guinness World Records.She became the oldest nun after the death of Brazil's Sister Inah Canabarro Lucas on April 30, 2025.
